leader.caveat: Includes 565,079 shares he votes but has no economic interest in.

structure.note: Class A has one vote per share and Class B ten. All Class B is held by the co-founders Vladimir Tenev and Baiju Bhatt and their related entities, who are parties to a Founders' Voting Agreement. The FY2024 10-K says they 'collectively with their related entities hold over 50% of the voting power of our outstanding capital stock' while holding about 14% of the common stock. The 2025 proxy gives Tenev 24.2% and Bhatt 35.9% of voting power. 'controlled' is true because the founders vote together under that agreement.

notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2024. Documents read on sec.gov: FY2024 Form 10-K (accession 0001783879-25-000049) and 2025 proxy statement (DEF 14A, accession 0001783879-25-000134). OWNERSHIP: the proxy gives percentages per class (Tenev 40.3% of Class B) and of voting power (24.2%), not of all shares, so the economic share is given only as leader.derived (5.28%). It counts all shares beneficially owned. Excluding the 565,079 Bhatt Family LLC shares, over which Tenev has voting but no economic interest, his own shares are 46,080,051 (6,907 Class A + 46,073,144 Class B). The Tenev 2017 Irrevocable Trust (6,808,231 Class B) and Butterfly Management LLC and Surfboard Management LLC (1,408,450 and 2,014,875 Class B), entities related to Tenev, are voted by Bhatt and appear only in Bhatt's row; they are not included. LARGEST HOLDERS left empty on purpose: The Vanguard Group (68,278,391 Class A, 8.9% of Class A, as of September 30, 2024) and FMR LLC (40,237,475 Class A, 5.2% of Class A, as of December 31, 2024) are stated only as percentages of Class A, and co-founder Baiju Bhatt (69,571,868 Class B, 60.2% of Class B, 35.9% of voting power) only per class. None is a share of all shares outstanding. BUYBACKS: $257 million of Class A repurchased in 2024. The $244 million of taxes paid on net share settlement of equity awards is excluded. GEOGRAPHY: null. Robinhood reports one operating segment and no revenue-by-geography table in the 10-K reviewed; the 10-K says its operations are concentrated in the United States.

ecosystem.notes: AUC is a stock, defined in the 10-K as: "We define AUC as the sum of the fair value of all equities, options, cryptocurrency, futures (including options on futures, swaps, and event contracts), and cash held by users in their accounts, net of receivables from users, as of a stated date or period end on a trade date basis." The 10-K defines Notional Trading Volume ("the aggregate dollar value (purchase price or sale price as applicable) of trades executed in that asset class over a specified period of time") but reports no annual dollar total for it, only growth in average volume per trader, so measure is null. The 10-K also reports Net Deposits of $50.5 billion for 2024; that is net client money moved onto the platform, not volume transacted through it, so it is not used as a measure. No take rate should be computed on AUC.
